issues.failure_explanation: The remark claims, citing Propositions~\ref{prop:boundary_inward_rank1} and \ref{prop:boundary_inward_rank1_approx}, that a GD step of any size η'∈(0,δ_t) maps ANY point of the level set {I(δ_t;·)=0} strictly into the interior of the sublevel set. The cited propositions establish strict inwardness only for boundary points outside the stationary set 𝒮 (their hypotheses read 'and (a_t,b_t,u_t,v_t) ∉ 𝒮', and their proofs conclude 'R_t(δ)<0 for every boundary point outside 𝒮', while showing R_t(δ)=0 on 𝒮∩{I(δ)=0}). Stationary boundary points exist in both settings: for I^fac, every global minimizer x_*=(a_*,b_*,0,0) with a_*b_*=1 lies on the level set with δ = 4/(a_*²+b_*²) ∈ (0,2], and the non-minimizing stationary axis points also lie on level sets; such points satisfy g_{η'}(x_*) = x_*, so I(δ;g_{η'}(x_*)) = I(δ;x_*) = 0 and the iterate is not mapped strictly into the interior. The remark's 'for any point' therefore asserts strictly more than the propositions establish, and the strengthened statement is false.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the qualifier used by the propositions themselves: replace 'for any point on the level set' by 'for any nonstationary point on the level set' (equivalently, add 'and (a_t,b_t,u_t,v_t) ∉ 𝒮'). No other content changes.
issues.overall_effect: The step-size-robustness statement in Remark rmk:inward_beyond_scalar is false as written for stationary boundary points; it holds only off the stationary set, exactly as the cited propositions state. No labelled convergence result depends on this remark, so the convergence guarantees of Section 3 are unaffected.
issues.title: Step-size-robustness remark drops the stationary-point exception
issues.why_classification: A local quantifier repair (excluding stationary boundary points, exactly as the cited propositions state) makes the remark correct; the inwardness mechanism, the step-size-robustness interpretation, and every substantive guarantee of the paper survive unchanged, so there is no mathematical loss.
